# 1. Load the package
library(lcmm)

# 2. To avoid local maxima, it is standard practice to first fit a 1-class model 
# to use as initial parameters (arguments) for multi-class models.
m1 <- Jointlcmm(fixed = eGFR ~ observation_time, 
                random = ~ observation_time, 
                subject = "patient_id",
                survival = Surv(time, status) ~ mixture(cohort), 
                hazard = "3-quant-splines", # flexible baseline hazard
                hazardtype = "CompetingRisks",
                data = main_dataset, 
                ng = 1)

# 3. Fit a 3-Class Joint Group-Based Model
# 'mixture(observation_time)' means the slope varies by group
# 'mixture(cohort)' lets your cohort variable alter survival risk by class
m3 <- Jointlcmm(fixed = eGFR ~ observation_time, 
                mixture = ~ observation_time,
                random = ~ observation_time, 
                subject = "patient_id",
                survival = Surv(time, status) ~ mixture(cohort), 
                hazard = "3-quant-splines",
                hazardtype = "CompetingRisks",
                data = main_dataset, 
                ng = 3, 
                B = m1) # Pass 1-class model parameters to initialize values

# 4. View model diagnostics
summary(m3)


# 1. Predict and plot the longitudinal eGFR paths for the 3 groups
# Generate data for a grid of time points
grid_time <- data.frame(observation_time = seq(0, 10, length.out = 100))

pred_trajectory <- predictY(m3, newdata = grid_time, var.time = "observation_time")
plot(pred_trajectory, lty = 1, lwd = 2, main = "Discovered eGFR Trajectory Groups")

# 2. Plot the cumulative risk of your competing endpoints by group
# This maps out the probability of experiencing ESKD vs Death for each of the 3 classes
plot(m3, which = "postprob", main = "Posterior Class Allocation Quality")
plot(m3, which = "hazard", main = "Cause-Specific Hazards Across Classes")


library(lcmm)

# Fit a 3-Class Joint Latent Class Model with Baseline Predictors
m3_with_covariates <- Jointlcmm(
  # 1. Longitudinal process (eGFR over time)
  fixed = eGFR ~ observation_time, 
  mixture = ~ observation_time,
  random = ~ observation_time, 
  subject = "patient_id",
  
  # 2. Class Membership Predictors 
  # These variables calculate the probability of a patient belonging to Class 1, 2, or 3
  classmb = ~ baseline_mental_health + baseline_bp + baseline_dm,
  
  # 3. Survival and Competing Risks configuration
  survival = Surv(time, status) ~ mixture(cohort), 
  hazard = "3-quant-splines",
  hazardtype = "CompetingRisks",
  
  # Data and Optimization configurations
  data = main_dataset, 
  ng = 3, 
  B = m1 # Pre-run 1-class model parameters to ensure stable convergence
)

# View model summary containing fixed effects, class predictors, and survival hazards
summary(m3_with_covariates)


# 1. View the overall distribution of patients across the 3 groups
# This tells you the sample size (N) and percentage share of each trajectory
postprob(m3_with_covariates)

# 2. Extract a clean dataset mapping each individual patient to their assigned class
# The model assigns patients to the class for which they have the highest posterior probability
patient_classes <- m3_with_covariates$pprob[, c("patient_id", "class")]

# View the first few rows
head(patient_classes)


# 1. Convert variables into explicit factors
main_dataset$baseline_dm <- factor(main_dataset$baseline_dm, 
                                   levels = c("No", "Yes"))

main_dataset$baseline_bp <- factor(main_dataset$baseline_bp, 
                                   levels = c("Normal", "Prehypertension", "Hypertension"))

main_dataset$baseline_mental_health <- factor(main_dataset$baseline_mental_health, 
                                              levels = c("None/Minimal", "Mild", "Moderate/Severe"))

# 2. Verify your formatting
str(main_dataset[, c("baseline_dm", "baseline_bp", "baseline_mental_health")])


library(lcmm)

m3_categorical <- Jointlcmm(
  fixed = eGFR ~ observation_time, 
  mixture = ~ observation_time,
  random = ~ observation_time, 
  subject = "patient_id",
  
  # Latent class membership predictors (now treated strictly as multi-level categories)
  classmb = ~ baseline_mental_health + baseline_bp + baseline_dm,
  
  survival = Surv(time, status) ~ mixture(cohort), 
  hazard = "3-quant-splines",
  hazardtype = "CompetingRisks",
  
  data = main_dataset, 
  ng = 3, 
  B = m1 # Initial parameter vector from your 1-class model
)


# 1. Extract the raw coefficients and variance-covariance matrix
estimates <- m3_categorical$best
se <- sqrt(diag(m3_categorical$V))

# 2. Filter specifically for the class membership parameters
# (Matches the rows containing your categorical baseline variables)
mb_rows <- grep("classmb", names(estimates))

or_table <- data.frame(
  Log_Odds = estimates[mb_rows],
  Odds_Ratio = exp(estimates[mb_rows]),
  Lower_95_CI = exp(estimates[mb_rows] - 1.96 * se[mb_rows]),
  Upper_95_CI = exp(estimates[mb_rows] + 1.96 * se[mb_rows]),
  p_value = 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(estimates[mb_rows] / se[mb_rows])))
)

# 3. View the clean clinical risk table
print(round(or_table, 3))
